seo.title: Google Business Profile Attributes: A Guide
seo.meta_description: Google Business Profile attributes for Anaheim and Orange County businesses: what they are, how to add them, accessibility attributes and review times.

h1: Google Business Profile Attributes: Show Customers What Matters
answer: Google Business Profile attributes are details such as Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, payment options and wheelchair accessibility that show on your profile in Search and Maps. Google says adding certain attributes can help your business show up in searches for places with those features. Edits are usually reviewed in about 10 minutes but can take up to 30 days. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should fill in every attribute that is true.
key_takeaways: Attributes show on Search and Maps.
They can match searches for those features.
Reviews take about 10 minutes, up to 30 days.

sections.heading: What attributes are
sections.body_html: Google's help page describes attributes as details that help your business stand out and tell customers what to expect, for example whether you offer outdoor seating or Wi-Fi. Attributes appear on your Business Profile on Search, Maps and other Google platforms.

sections.heading: Why they matter
sections.body_html: Google says that if you add certain attributes, your business might show up in searches for places with those attributes. Someone in Anaheim looking for a wheelchair-accessible restaurant or a cafe with Wi-Fi is effectively filtering by attributes.

sections.heading: How to add or edit attributes
sections.body_html: Go to your Business Profile, select Edit profile, then More. Next to the category you want, such as Amenities or Payments, select Edit, choose Yes or No for each attribute, and save. Google notes that some attributes can only be changed in certain locations, countries or business categories.

sections.heading: Attributes customers provide
sections.body_html: Google says some attributes may be populated from customers who visit your business. Check your profile regularly and correct anything that is no longer accurate.

sections.heading: Review times
sections.body_html: Google says a review of attribute edits usually takes about 10 minutes but can sometimes take up to 30 days. It also notes attribute names may change over time to match how people search.

sections.heading: Accessibility attributes
sections.body_html: Google defines accessibility attributes precisely. For example, select Yes for a wheelchair-accessible entrance if the entrance is three feet or one meter wide with no steps, or has a ramp; select No if the entrance is only revolving doors. Restrooms, seating and parking have their own definitions, and hearing assistance options include assisted listening devices, hearing loops and Auracast broadcasters.

sections.heading: Be accurate
sections.body_html: Only select attributes that are true. A customer who arrives expecting accessible parking or Wi-Fi that is not there will not come back, and may leave a review saying so.

sections.heading: Attributes by business type
sections.body_html:
• Restaurants and cafes: outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, reservations, dietary options.
  • Retail: payment types, accessibility, delivery or pickup.
  • Health and beauty: accessibility, appointment requirements.
  • Service businesses: payment options, online estimates where offered.

sections.heading: Attributes and your website
sections.body_html: Repeat important details, such as accessibility and payment options, on your website. Consistency helps Google and AI assistants answer customers' practical questions about your business.

sections.heading: Check them regularly
sections.body_html: Review attributes when anything changes: new payment methods, renovations, new seating or services. Seasonal changes, such as patio seating, should be updated too.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Amenities set.
  • Payment options set.
  • Accessibility attributes checked against Google's definitions.
  • Customer-provided attributes reviewed.
  • Seasonal attributes updated.
  • Key details repeated on the website.

sections.heading: Common attribute mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Leaving most attributes blank, so the profile says nothing about payments, accessibility or amenities.
  • Selecting attributes that are only partly true, such as accessible parking that is often unavailable.
  • Forgetting to update attributes after a renovation, a new payment system or the end of patio season.
  • Not checking details that customers have contributed to the profile.
  • Describing amenities on the profile that the website contradicts.

sections.heading: Attributes customers in Orange County ask about
sections.body_html: The attributes that matter depend on who your customers are. Families visiting Anaheim often look for accessible entrances, restrooms and seating; diners compare outdoor seating, reservations and dietary options; shoppers want to know which payment methods are accepted; and people booking services want to know whether appointments are needed. Think about the questions your staff answer on the phone every week, then check that each answer is reflected in your attributes where Google offers one. Every question answered on the profile is one less reason for a customer to choose a competitor whose profile answers it first.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a coffee shop in Costa Mesa that adds outdoor seating and starts accepting contactless payments. The owner opens Edit profile, More, and updates Amenities and Payments, then measures the entrance to confirm it meets Google's wheelchair-accessible definition before selecting Yes. The website's visit page is updated with the same details.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: Treat this as part of a routine rather than a one-off fix. Local visibility in Anaheim and the rest of Orange County comes from many small, accurate signals adding up: a verified profile, consistent listings, useful service pages, real photos and a flow of honest reviews. Google is open that relevance, distance and popularity drive local results. You cannot change distance, but you can make sure Google and AI assistants understand exactly what you do and see evidence that customers value it. Put a monthly reminder in the calendar to check the profile, read new reviews and update anything that has changed.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask why an attribute they set is not showing. Some attributes only appear for certain categories or regions, and edits can take time to review, so check again after a few days. Another common question is whether attributes replace a good description. They do not: attributes answer specific yes-or-no questions, while the description and services explain what you do. Owners also ask whether to select attributes that apply only part of the time. Choose the answer that is true for a typical visit, and use special hours or updates to explain temporary changes.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Open Edit profile, then More.
  2. Go through every attribute category.
  3. Check accessibility definitions carefully.
  4. Update your website to match.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: You do not need an agency for every step here; Google documents most of it clearly. Consider outside help when the work is urgent and unfamiliar, when you manage several locations, or when the same issue returns after you fix it. Ask any provider to show you the specific guideline or documentation behind each recommendation, to keep you as the owner of your accounts and to report results in calls, bookings and leads rather than vanity numbers. That is how Chimera works with Orange County businesses from our base in Anaheim.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Fill in every true attribute, use Google's definitions for accessibility, recheck after changes and mirror key details on your website. Chimera, based in Anaheim, completes attributes in every Orange County profile audit.

faqs.q: What are Google Business Profile attributes?
faqs.a: Details like Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, payments and accessibility shown on your profile.
Google says adding certain attributes may help you show up in searches for places with those attributes.

faqs.q: How long do attribute edits take?
faqs.a: Usually about 10 minutes, but sometimes up to 30 days.
Some attributes may be populated from customer input; check and correct them.

faqs.q: What counts as a wheelchair-accessible entrance?
faqs.a: Google says an entrance three feet or one meter wide with no steps, or with a ramp.

faqs.q: Why can't I see some attributes?
faqs.a: Some are only available in certain locations, countries or categories.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
